quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When it is dawn, dusk, raining, or snowing, it is hard to see and be seen. What should you turn on to let other drivers know you are there?
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers may not be able to see you. Use your low beam headlights when you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to leave the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.

questions.explanation: When it is dark or the weather is bad, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to stop if you see a hazard.

questions.question: When you park facing uphill on a road with no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right toward the edge of the road. If the brakes fail, your car will roll off the road safely.

questions.question: In Nebraska, what is the blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit for drivers under 21?
questions.explanation: In Nebraska, drivers under 21 cannot drive with a BAC of 0.02 percent or higher.

questions.question: On the interstate, where should slower traffic drive?
questions.explanation: Slower traffic should stay on the right side of the interstate. The left lane is for faster-moving vehicles to pass slower ones.

questions.question: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers and must follow all traffic laws.
questions.explanation: In Nebraska, bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers and must obey all traffic laws. Drivers should respect bicyclists' right to use the road.

questions.question: When turning or stopping in rain, you should be most careful:

options.text: After it has rained all day.
One half hour after the rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars mixes with the rain and makes the road slippery.

questions.question: When turning, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning so you can control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to surprises.

questions.question: Fines for speeding in work zones are:
questions.explanation: Fines for speeding are doubled in work zones where workers are present and in school zones during certain hours. Drive carefully near workers, children, and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. The railroad tracks cross the road at a steep angle. Low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: What happens to a bicyclist who breaks traffic laws?

options.text: They are right because bicyclists don't have to obey traffic laws.
They will always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as car drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: How do sudden wind gusts affect highway driving?
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can blow dirt and dust onto the road, reducing visibility. Wind can also physically push a vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if it is open.
If no right lane is open, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce speed to let them pass you.

questions.explanation: If someone tailgates you, move right if possible. If you cannot move right, wait for a clear road ahead and reduce speed slowly. Never brake suddenly because this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look for other traffic, and continue carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns of a curve in the road.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Return to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in any lane you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, return to the right side when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: How can you help prevent being hit from behind?

options.text: Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots.
Release the gas and let your car slow before using the brakes.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. Release the gas to let your vehicle slow, then apply steady brake pressure. This activates your brake lights and stops your car smoothly.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in rain?
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: Must a driver turning left yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction?
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must leave a note on the vehicle you hit. Include your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: When driving on a slippery surface like snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Maintain traction by following other vehicles closely.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before going down a steep hill to prevent skidding. Stay farther behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid quick stops. If you do not have antilock brakes, pump the brakes to slow down.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake immediately. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slowly release the accelerator. Once you are moving slowly, apply the brakes gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the roadway edge, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the roadway.
Turn back onto the roadway immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the roadway.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back immediately. Slow down, check traffic, and gradually turn back onto the roadway when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods of time.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside them for long periods.
